benefits: Covers the five most-used 3D shapes: cube, cuboid, sphere, cylinder and cone.
Shows the exact formula result with full precision — no rounding surprises.
Bonus details like slant height and lateral area are computed automatically.
Works with any unit: mm, cm, m, in or ft.
Runs entirely in your browser; nothing is uploaded.

faqs.a: Surface area is the total area of all outer faces of a 3D shape, measured in square units (cm², m²...). Volume, by contrast, measures the space inside, in cubic units.
faqs.q: What is the difference between surface area and volume?

faqs.a: Because the curved surface unwraps into a rectangle of width 2πr (the circumference) and height h, plus the two circular bases: 2πr² + 2πrh = 2πr(r + h).
faqs.q: Why is the cylinder formula 2πr(r + h)?

faqs.a: The slant height l = √(r² + h²) is the distance from the tip to the base edge along the slope. The lateral (side) area is πrl, and adding the base πr² gives πr(r + l).
faqs.q: What is the slant height of a cone?

faqs.a: A cube has 6 identical square faces, each of area a², so the total is 6a². A cuboid's faces come in three different pairs, hence 2(lw + lh + wh).
faqs.q: Why is a cube 6a² but a cuboid 2(lw + lh + wh)?

faqs.a: Yes — the unit selector changes only the label on the result. It does not convert between units; enter all dimensions in the same unit you select.
faqs.q: Can I use inches or feet instead of cm?

surface-area-calculator.formula:
Cube:     SA = 6a²
Cuboid:   SA = 2(lw + lh + wh)
Sphere:   SA = 4πr²
Cylinder: SA = 2πr² + 2πrh = 2πr(r + h)
Cone:     SA = πr² + πrl = πr(r + l),  where l = √(r² + h²) is the slant height
howTo: Choose the 3D shape from the dropdown.
Enter its dimensions — every value in the same unit.
Pick the unit label (mm, cm, m, in, ft) for the result.
Read the total surface area, shown in square units.
Check the bonus row for face area, lateral area or slant height where available.
keyFacts: Surface area is always measured in square units (cm², m², in²...).
A sphere has the smallest surface area of any shape enclosing a given volume.
Doubling every dimension quadruples the surface area (the square-cube scaling).
The cone's slant height comes from Pythagoras: l = √(r² + h²).
Paint, wrapping paper and material estimates all start from surface area.

limitations: Only the five listed shapes are supported — irregular shapes need numerical methods.
All dimensions must use the same unit; the tool does not convert between units.
Results assume perfect geometric shapes; real objects have seams and thickness.
Display rounds to 8 significant digits; the underlying math uses full precision.

surface-area-calculator.quickAnswer: Pick a shape and enter its dimensions — for example a sphere of radius 3 cm gives 4π × 9 = 113.097 cm². Cube, cuboid, cylinder and cone are supported, in mm, cm, m, in or ft.
surface-area-calculator.tagline: Surface areas of cubes, cuboids, spheres, cylinders and cones.
surface-area-calculator.workedExample:
Sphere with radius r = 3 cm:
SA = 4πr² = 4 × π × 3² = 4 × π × 9 = 36π ≈ 113.097 cm²

Cylinder with r = 2 cm, h = 5 cm:
SA = 2πr(r + h) = 2 × π × 2 × (2 + 5) = 4π × 7 = 28π ≈ 87.965 cm²
Lateral area = 2πrh = 2 × π × 2 × 5 = 20π ≈ 62.832 cm²
